# Biological Specimens
[color=#a4885c]RESTRICTED. Research staff only. Do not discuss the contents of this section with anyone who isn't cleared for it, including other Company employees.[/color]
The frontier is home to organisms that science has barely begun to understand. Some of them are dangerous. All of them are of great scientific and medical interest to the Company, and from time to time you may be asked to study one.
You're being told about these organisms so you can recognise them and stay safe, not so you can go looking for them.
## Organisms of interest - [bold]XX-121 ("Xenomorph")[/bold]: a hostile organism that builds hive colonies. Its blood is a powerful acid that eats through most materials, so it must never be cut or shot near equipment you want to keep. It reproduces through a parasitic larval stage. Any larva, egg or parasite must be treated as a live and dangerous specimen. - [bold]Biomorph tissue[/bold]: an aggressive, self-organising mass of flesh that spreads through venom and spores. Any sample of biomorph tissue or venom is an infection risk. Handle it only in sealed containers and full protective equipment. - [bold]Variant organisms[/bold]: the Company has recorded several related or unusual forms, including the [bold]Neomorph[/bold] and the large predator known as the [bold]Wendigo[/bold]. Treat any unfamiliar creature as dangerous until the Lead Researcher says otherwise.
## Handling live specimens - [bold]Never approach a live specimen.[/bold] Live specimens are collected and moved by specialist Company teams, not by research staff. - A specimen delivered to the lab arrives sedated and restrained in a secure specimen crate. Don't open the crate unless the Lead Researcher tells you to, and never with only one person present. - Keep a sedated specimen sedated. If it starts to move, step back, seal the area and call Security. - Dead specimens and tissue samples are still hazardous. Acid blood stays active after death, and biomorph tissue can still infect.
## Samples and records - Every sample is logged, labelled and stored under lock. - Specimen data is never saved anywhere outside the lab. - Destroy unused samples only on the Lead Researcher's instruction, and record that you did.
## Keeping the public calm Colonists aren't aware that these organisms exist, and it's important that it stays that way. News of a dangerous creature causes panic, and panic costs lives. If a colonist asks about something they've seen, tell them it's under investigation and refer them to the Corporate Liaison.
The Company's work with these organisms is carried out for the benefit of science and medicine. Questions about the wider programme should be put to the Lead Researcher, who will answer them as far as your clearance allows.
